newsitem.title: INDIA: Enron calls Indian oilfield bidding fair.
newsitem.headline: Enron calls Indian oilfield bidding fair.

text.p: U.S.-based Enron Oil & Gas Co (EOG) said on Monday that the bidding process for two Indian offshore oilfields, under government investigation, was fair and in line with Indian law.

EOG said in statement released in the Indian capital that "it remains confident the bidding process for the Panna and Mukta fields offshore India was conducted fairly and in accordance with Indian law".

It said "EOG believes the bid, which was the highest bid submitted for the Panna/Mukta fields in a competitive bidding process, was awarded on its merit alone, following due deliberation of all parties involved, including the Government of India and the Oil and Natural Gas Corp," it added.
Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) is an oil exploration company controlled by the Indian government. EOG is a subsidiary of U.S.-based Enron Corp.

EOG's statement followed a government announcement last week that an inquiry had been ordered into the manner in which drilling contracts for three oilfields, including the Panna and Mukta fields, were awarded to private firms.

Junior Petroleum Minister T.R. Baalu said last week that federal police had launched a preliminary enquiry into the contracts for the Panna and Mukta oilfields in western India and the Ravva oilfield in southwestern India.
The Panna and Mukta fields were awarded in October 1994 to a joint venture linking Enron Oil & Gas India Ltd, which is an affiliate of EOG, and India's Reliance Industries Ltd.
The Panna and Mukta fields are part of the Bombay Offshore basin in western India. Enron Oil and Gas India Ltd and Reliance signed the contract to drill for oil in the two fields in December 1994.

The Ravva oil field contract was awarded to a consortium linking Videocon Petroleum Ltd, which is a unit of Videocon International Ltd, Cairn Energy Plc's Australian unit Command Petroleum Ltd and Japan's Marubeni Corp .
